description: The FILE file-name-1 alternative of WRITE and REWRITE ({ record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1 } FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 }, Annex A.4.13 items 1 and 2) - the record released is the FROM operand under the description of the operand (the implicit record of §2023:14.9.51.4 GR8 / §2023:14.9.35.4 GR9). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): X3.23-1985 prints `WRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ]` (§1985:VII.4.7.2) and `REWRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ END-REWRITE ]` (§1985:VII.4.5.2) only; §2002:14.8.47.1 and §2002:14.8.33.1 print `{ record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1 }`, §2002:14.8.47.2 SR7 and §2002:14.8.33.2 SR10 require 'If the FILE phrase is specified, the FROM phrase shall also be specified', §2002:14.8.47.3 GR5 and §2002:14.8.33.3 GR8 give the meaning ('The result of execution of a WRITE statement with the FILE phrase is equivalent to the execution of the following'), and §2002:F.2 item 149 states the change: 'Writing without a record-name. A FILE phrase on the WRITE and REWRITE statements permit writing records from working storage without having a corresponding record description entry in the file section' (item 148 the literal operand: 'Using the FILE phrase of WRITE, alphanumeric, national, and boolean literals and the figurative constant SPACE can be written'). §2014:14.9.47.2 SR7, §2014:14.9.33.2 SR9, §2014:14.9.47.3 GR6 and §2014:14.9.33.3 GR8 keep it, so 2014 = 2023. kb/Work PB5579. Gated in ONE place, VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitWriteStatement / VisitRewriteStatement.
display: the FILE phrase of a WRITE or REWRITE statement
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. VMWRF.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN TO "VMWRF" ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R PIC X(5).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 W PIC X(5) VALUE "NEW01".
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           OPEN OUTPUT F.
           WRITE FILE F FROM W.
           CLOSE F.
           STOP RUN.
